finding.cause: prepared-apply commits the domain receipt with additionalNamespaces: cases. The state provider increments every write namespace, although this callback only reads the case. createPreparedExecution then reconciles using the cases storageVersion captured before that commit.
finding.effect: The first domain application can commit its mutation and durable receipt, then return unavailable/case-reconciliation-pending. Exact retry reads the bound receipt and can reconcile without repeating the domain mutation when the case remains unchanged.
finding.truthToPreserve: A pending case reconciliation does not establish that the domain was not applied. Preserve the durable receipt and the observed domain-applied fact across a late failure. Never reset it to false or repeat the mutation solely because the outer result is unavailable.

proposedDelta.behavior: After observing the durable receipt and before reconciling, reread the case under current authority. Require its full digest to equal the original case observation, revalidate case/application authority, and use the fresh cases storageVersion. The transaction still checks the case version, incarnation, authority and current namespace CAS.
proposedDelta.reason: This preserves prepared-apply write authority, transaction scopeDigest and persisted receipt identities. It only refreshes the reconciliation CAS after the known domain transaction.
proposedDelta.alternativeNotApplied: Changing prepared-apply additionalNamespaces: cases to checkNamespaces: cases also prevents the version increment, but changes case authority from write to read and transaction scopeDigest. WP11 must assess grants and exact retry compatibility before choosing this alternative.

consumerRegression.test: portfolio handoff prepares two WP11 changes and resumes a partial application without repeating a receipt
consumerRegression.implementation: Uses createDecisionMutations, createSfPreparedApply, createPreparedExecution, receiptReviewBinding/proposalReviewDigest and real local-store persistence. The domain mutation callback is a controlled synthetic amount field in Planner and Procurement snapshots; this is not proof of canonical domain-engine execution or the UI/native human flow.
consumerRegression.currentPinExpectation: Assert first application returns case-reconciliation-pending while the durable receipt and Planner amount are already committed. Retry exactly, fail Procurement before mutation, and resume it; Planner mutation count must remain one.
consumerRegression.afterOwnerDelta: WP11 must publish its selected fix and update first-call assertions to success while retaining a separate forced late-reconciliation-failure test and exact receipt replay checks.
consumerRegression.runStatus: NOT_RUN_LOCALLY; await root surgical GitHub Actions run

requiredOwnerChecks: Fresh first application returns a reconciled receipt without requiring an automatic retry solely for its own namespace increment.
A concurrent case content/version change after domain commit returns reconciliation pending and never overwrites the newer case.
Late authority revocation preserves durable truth, withholds unauthorized receipt disclosure, and does not repeat the domain mutation on a later authorized retry.
Exact replay validates the review digest, command digest, target incarnation, receipt identity and persisted proof; changed content or review cannot reuse the receipt.
Partial Planner/Procurement application resumes only the unapplied change and leaves previously applied domain data unchanged.
nextAction: WP11 reviews and publishes the delta with its surgical hosted receipt/application tests. WP13 then consumes the published pin and reruns only the affected handoff consumer. S0 decides integration; no READY claim follows from this receipt.
